questions.stem:
The balanced delta load shown is connected to a stable, three-phase voltage source. The rms line voltage is 120 V. The load impedance per phase is 15 Ω + j10 Ω.

![Delta load circuit diagram](/images/ch26-q1-delta-load-circuit.png)

What is most nearly the rms magnitude of the line current?
questions.explanation: For a delta connection, V_phase = V_line = 120 V. Phase impedance magnitude |Z| = √(15² + 10²) ≈ 18.028 Ω. Phase current I_phase = V_phase / |Z| = 120 / 18.028 ≈ 6.656 A. Line current I_line = √3 × I_phase = √3 × 6.656 ≈ 11.53 A. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

questions.stem: A 240 V ∠0° source supplies a balanced, three-phase load in a delta configuration. The line current is 3 A ∠45°. What is most nearly the magnitude of the complex power measured across the load?
questions.explanation: Total complex power magnitude |S| = √3 × V_line × I_line = √3 × 240 V × 3 A ≈ 1247 VA ≈ 1200 VA. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

questions.stem: A balanced, three-phase, delta-connected system has three identical phase impedances. The line-to-line voltage is 240 V. The line current is 41 A. Most nearly, the magnitudes of the phase voltage and phase current in the system are:
questions.explanation: In a delta connection, phase voltage equals line voltage (V_phase = 240 V). Phase current is line current divided by √3 (I_phase = 41 A / √3 ≈ 23.67 A). The answer is (D).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

questions.stem:
A balanced, three-phase, wye-connected load system has three identical phase impedances of 40 Ω − j30 Ω. Most nearly, the equivalent delta-connected phase impedances are:

![Wye-connected load circuit diagram](/images/ch26-q4-wye-load-circuit.png)
questions.explanation: To convert from wye to delta, Z_delta = 3 × Z_wye = 3 × (40 Ω − j30 Ω) = 120 Ω − j90 Ω. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

questions.stem: A balanced, three-phase, wye-connected system has three identical phase impedances. The line-to-line voltage is 240 V. The line-to-neutral current is 41 A. The power factor is 0.8 leading. Most nearly, the total apparent power in the system is:
questions.explanation: Total apparent power S = √3 × V_line × I_line × (pf − j·sin(acos(pf))). S = √3 × 240 × 41 ≈ 17043 VA ≈ 17 kVA. Real power P = 17 kVA × 0.8 = 13.6 kW ≈ 14 kW. Reactive power Q is negative for leading (capacitive) loads. Q = -17 kVA × sin(acos(0.8)) = -17 × 0.6 = -10.2 kVAR ≈ -10 kVAR. S = 14 kW - j10 kVA. The answer is (C).
questions.reference: FE Reference Handbook – Power, Three-Phase Circuits

puzzle_instance.narrative: Fill in the crossword puzzle using the clues related to three-phase power.

words.clue: Complex AC opposition; Z = R + jX, units in ohms
Triangle three-phase load connection; V_phase = V_line
One of three branches; voltage or current per branch
Impedance that consumes power in the circuit
Unit of real (active) power; P = I²R
Rate of energy transfer; P = VI·cos(θ) in AC systems
